benefits.title: Students can expect experiential learning to become a deliberate feature of a King's education
benefits.statement: King's establishes a clear institutional ambition for the experiential learning students should encounter through their education, with an explicit future entitlement that can guide subsequent curriculum growth, near-curriculum provision and investment. The entitlement is developed as a forward institutional commitment rather than presented as already achieved in Year 1.
benefits.benefitType: educational entitlement, equity and student development
benefits.successLooksLike: Students and course teams can understand the direction of travel for experiential learning at King's, and subsequent implementation decisions can be tested against a clear and credible student entitlement rather than a collection of unrelated local initiatives.

benefits.title: King's can expand experiential learning consistently, inclusively and with impact
benefits.statement: Educators, programme teams and professional services can draw on a shared theoretical and design basis for experiential learning, including a common typology, learning-design and reflection principles, experientially aligned assessment approaches, reusable delivery models and quality expectations. This reduces repeated local redesign and creates a common basis for inclusive growth and assurance.
benefits.beneficiary: Educators, programme teams, faculties and professional services
benefits.benefitType: institutional capability, inclusive growth and effective use of resource
benefits.successLooksLike: Teams developing experiential learning can use and adapt shared institutional models with confidence. Downstream investment, operating support and curriculum growth align with the North Star; unnecessary reinvention is reduced; and new provision is designed from the outset around educational purpose, accessibility, quality and evidence of impact.

benefits.title: King's establishes a distinctive position of thought and practice leadership
benefits.statement: King's develops a recognised intellectual and practical contribution to experiential learning at a point when the sector is rapidly converging on an insufficiently interrogated consensus centred on employability, placements and visible volumes of activity. By coalescing existing expertise, testing its ideas through institutional practice and sharing what it learns, King's can offer a richer and more educationally credible account of experiential learning.
benefits.beneficiary: King's, its academic and professional community, students, external partners and the wider higher education sector
benefits.benefitType: thought leadership, external influence and institutional reputation
benefits.successLooksLike: King's scholarship, framework and institutional experience are visible in sector debate, generate external engagement and collaboration, and influence how experiential learning is understood and developed beyond the University.
